"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;MY INTERNSHIP JOURNEY IN GENERAL MEDICINE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI'm an intern, posted in general medicine department for 2 months including 2 weeks of psychiatry.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFirst 2 weeks:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPosted in Department of Psychiatry:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAttended the OPD in department of psychiatry and observed various spectrum of psychiatric disorders in the patients. Studied symptomatology regarding various psychiatric disorder spectrums.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI got to know about the ICD-10 Classification of psychiatry disorders and also DSM Classification of diseases.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDone night duties for observation of psychiatry patients of withdrawal syndromes. And learnt how to manage them.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAttended the De addiction centre visits and observed the various types of medical, behavioural therapy going on there.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELearnt how to attend rounds for the patients and how to write repeats in the casesheets from post graduates.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETyped, studied and submitted the discharge summaries of various patients under department of psychiatry. From this I learnt how to discharge a patient with proper counselling required and proper instructions for medications for both patients and attenders.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4 WEEKS OF UNIT DUTIES:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI was posted in the unit-I in the successive 4 weeks.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMy first day in unit was our op day. I learnt how to take op cases with proper history and examination and how to investigate and how to manage the treatment part with proper counselling.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdmitted patients who required further management under supervision.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAll investigations required and recommended by post graduates, senior residents and faculty had been sent and samples drawn, collected and sent for laboratory.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStudied venous sampling. Performed venous sampling.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELearnt ABG sampling and learnt ABG interpretation from post graduates. Clarified doubts.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELearnt basics of ECG. Interpretation of chest x ray.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFoleys catheterization done for 5 patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERyles tube insertion done for 4 patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECompleted fever charts in the casesheets and filled investigation charts up to date everyday.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUpdated SOAP NOTES for every patient in their PAJR groups created by us.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECreated PAJR groups for every patient admitted\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECreated blogs of all patients with consent from patients and \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDischarge Date\n\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDate:20\/03\/2023\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiagnosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHYPOXIC ISCHEMIC ENCEPHALOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ES\/P TRACHEOSTOMY WITH K\/C\/O SEIZURE DISORDER\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECase History and Clinical Findings:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPATIENT IS IN VEGETATIVE STATE FOR PAST 8-9 MONTHS AND TRACHEOSTOMY WS DONE. IN 2019, HE HAD ONCE C\/O LEFT UPPER QUADRANT ABDOMINAL PAIN WHEN THE PAINI NTENSIFIED HE WAS TAKEN RO LOCAL HOSPITAL, GOT ADMITTED FOR 2 DAYS AND DISCHARGED. NO SUCH INCIDENT AFTER DISCHARGE 9 MONTHS AGO, ONE LATE NIGHT AT AROUND 10PM, HIS FRIEND DROPPED HIM 800 METRES AWAY FROM HOME NEAR A LAMP PEAT AFTER HEAVY DRINKING WITH HIS FRIENDS 5 MINUTES LATER HIS FRIEND SAW PATIENT IS HUGGING THE LAMP PEAT TIGHTLY. HE WAS NOT REPLYING WHEN HE CALLED THE PATIENT. SO WHEN HE TRIED TO TOUCH THE PATIENT, HE GOT AN ELECTRIC SHOCK. REALIZING PATIENT HAD BEEN ELECTROCUTED HE CALLED HIS ANOTHER FRIENDS AND THEY TOOK HIM TO THE HOSPITAL. HE WAS UNCOSCIOUS UPON REACHING THE HOSPITAL CPR WAS GIVEN AND VENTILATION DONE. DOCTOR SAID THAT HE IS IN VEGETATIVE STATE AND REFERRED HIM TO ANOTHER HOSPITAL. THERE IN THAT HOSPITAL TRACHEOSTOMY WAS DONE AND HE STAYED IN THE HOSPITAL FOR 45 DAYS. BY THAT TIME HE WAS ABLE TO MOVE HIS FINGERS SLIGHTLY. DOCTOR SAID NOTHING MORE CAN BE DONE AND GOT DISCHARGED. HE WAS ADMITTED TO ANOTHER HOSPITAL, WHERE HE STAYED TO DATE. IN THE PAST 9 MONTHS TILL DATE, SLOWLY HE IS ABLE TO BLINK HIS EYES, MAKE EYE CONTACT, GRIP SOMEONE'S FINGER. HE IS TRYING TO LIFT HIS HEAD. FOR THE PAST 2-3 MONTHS HE IS ABLE TO SIP WATER WHEN FED VIA SPOON. STILL BEING FED VIA RYLES TUBE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPAST HISTORY:N\/K\/C\/O DM, HTN, TB, BA, CAD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETRACHEOSTOMY DONE 9 MONTHS AGO\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY; REGULAR ALCOHOLIC\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGENERAL PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAT ADMISSION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENO SIGNS OF PALLOR, ICTERUS, CLUBBING, CYANOSIS, GENERALISED\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELYMPHADENOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBP 110\/80MMHG\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPR 110BPM\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERR 22CPM\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETEMP AFEBRILE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESPO2 99% ON RA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ES1 AND S2 HEARD. NO MURMURS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERESPIRATORY SYSTEM: BAE PRESENT, CLEAR\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGCS:E3V2M4\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPUPILS REACTING\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECORNEAL AND CONJUCTIVAL REFLEX PRESENT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETONE;
